public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 653

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/653](https://www.erdosproblems.com/653)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Finset EuclideanGeometry Filter

namespace Erdos653

/-- Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $R(x_i)=\#\{ \lvert x_j-x_i\rvert : j\neq i\}$,
where the points are ordered such that
$$R(x_1)\leq \cdots \leq R(x_n).$$
Let $g(n)$ be the maximum number of distinct values the $R(x_i)$ can take. Is it true that
$g(n) \geq (1-o(1))n$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem erdos_653 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (1 - o n) * n ≤ maximalDistinctDistancesFrom n := by
  sorry

end Erdos653

review.notes:
The sole declaration, Erdos653.erdos_653, faithfully states the source's question. distinctDistancesFrom excludes the base point and counts distinct distances; the outer image counts distinct values of these counts. Ordering the points is immaterial. The supremum ranges over a nonempty set of natural numbers bounded by n, so it is an attained maximum, not a default-value case.

The sorry-free scratch file /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without warnings or errors. It verifies boundedness and attainment, g(0)=0, g(1)=1, g(2)=1, and equivalence of the theorem's right-hand side to g(n)/n tending to 1. The answer slot has the correct scope and polarity.

The live source returned HTTP 403. Source comparison used archived captures, most recently 2026-08-24. That capture and the currently retrieved Erdős-problems database both record the problem as open; no status discrepancy was found.
